sentence_stem: Not only had the novelist rewritten the final chapter,
correct_completion: but she had also changed the title.
full_sentence: Not only had the novelist rewritten the final chapter, but she had also changed the title.
acceptable_variants: but she had also reconsidered the entire plot.
but she had also revised the dedication.

options.text: and then she left for a holiday.
options.why_wrong: Simple coordination does not complete the 'not only ... but also' correlative structure, which requires an additive emphatic continuation.

so the editor refused the manuscript.
options.why_wrong: 'So' introduces a result, which conflicts with the additive emphasis set up by 'not only'.
'Although' signals concession and contradicts the additive pattern that the stem sets up.

grammar_focus: Correlative conjunction 'not only ... but also' with subject-auxiliary inversion
explanation: After 'not only', the sentence uses inversion, with the auxiliary placed before the subject. The second clause must introduce an additional action marked by 'but also'. Learners may find this structure unfamiliar because it relies on a fixed correlative pair rather than a single connecting word.
